subject: Peregrine demo — temporary dedicated capacity and autoscale exception
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Peregrine demo — temporary dedicated capacity and autoscale exception

Marcus —

We have a high-visibility Peregrine Health demo scheduled for the week of Nov 29 (customer execs + engineering). They want a live inference demo using their fine-tuned 7B model and Redwood dedicated routing to demonstrate latency under load. Product would like a temporary dedicated slice with an autoscale exception so we can burst to 16 GPUs for a 48-hour window around the demo (roughly Nov 29–30).

Key numbers:
- Model: 7B fine-tuned (4-bit quantized)
- Expected steady qps: 40
- Peak qps during scripted load tests: 220 (short bursts)
- Estimated tokens per minute (peak): ~1.2M
- Duration: 48 hours + 4h pre-flight and 2h postmortem

Ask: Can infra provision either a temporary dedicated pool (preferred) or grant an autoscale soft-exception on the pilot pool so we can burst without eviction? We need pricing/ops confirmation by EOD Thu 11/11 to confirm with customer.

I've attached a rough capacity plan (20271109_demo_capacity_plan.xlsx) with a cost sketch. Please advise:
1) Which option minimises risk to other pilots?
2) What runbooks/alerts do you want in place for oncall?
3) Any encryption/KMS or VPC routing concerns for Peregrine?

Thanks — I can take the follow-up with the customer once we have tradeoffs.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Peregrine demo — temporary dedicated capacity and autoscale exception

Laura —

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifying questions before I can commit:
1) Is the model pinned to a specific instance type (A100/H100 family)? If it's H100-only we have fewer spare slots.
2) Are we required to keep KV caches warm between bursts (i.e., long tail of session affinity)? That impacts memory footprint significantly.
3) Is Peregrine in scope for customer-managed KMS (we should understand egress for HSM access if so).

Options I see:
A) Temporary dedicated pool (recommended): carve 16 GPUs from pilot buffer and mark as "demo-slice-20271129". This isolates risk but requires a short reallocation and Ops approval for the carve.
B) Autoscale soft-exception on pilot pool: allow burst above hard cap for 48h with backpressure fallback to a 7B distill variant. Lower isolation, faster to enable.

Initial impact calc attached (pool_impact_calc.csv). Roughly, option A increases committed monthly consumption by ~0.5 node-months prorated; option B may increase transient utilization by ~3–4x during the window and risk evictions on adjacent pilots if we mis-schedule.

If Marissa can sign off on provisional cost treatment we can proceed with option A and I will schedule the carving next Tuesday to give 48h lead time. Hannah — for oncall, do you want a dedicated escalation path for the demo (pager + Slack channel)?

I will hold until you confirm model instance and KMS details.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Peregrine demo — temporary dedicated capacity and autoscale exception

Looping in a quick customer note — Anna at Peregrine confirmed they need the demo to be "production-like" (low single-digit token latency under scripted load). They asked specifically for an isolated slice to avoid cross-tenant interference.

Customer contacts:
- Anna Gomez (procurement/ops): anna@peregrinehealth.com
- Infra alias: eng+infra@peregrinehealth.com

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/PH-4821 — Peregrine is moving toward a pilot PO; if we can promise an isolated demo environment and a clear overage policy they are more likely to issue a PO quickly.

From a sales perspective, option A (temporary dedicated pool) is materially preferable. If Ops needs a short cost buffer we can try to push some of the demo costs into the upcoming pilot commitment as an accommodation.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — summary and next steps below.

On Fri, Nov 12, 2027 at 11:02 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Laura —
>
> Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifying questions before I can commit:
> 1) Is the model pinned to a specific instance type (A100/H100 family)? If it's H100-only we have fewer spare slots.
> 2) Are we required to keep KV caches warm between bursts (i.e., long tail of session affinity)? That impacts memory footprint significantly.
> 3) Is Peregrine in scope for customer-managed KMS (we should understand egress for HSM access if so).

Answers inline:
- Model: can run on A100 flex v2; Peregrine confirmed no H100 mandate.
- KV cache: not required between distinct scripted sessions; warm cache for sustained sessions only. We'll plan for cache-warm preflight.
- KMS: Peregrine is asking for CMK but can accept our managed key for the demo; no HSM egress required.

Action items:
1) Marcus to provision temporary dedicated pool "demo-slice-20271129" (16 GPUs, A100 family) and share a final cost estimate by 2027-11-15 EOD.
2) Hannah to stand up an oncall rota and a dedicated Slack channel + pager for Nov 28–Dec 1.
3) Ben to confirm customer PO timeline and share legal/commercial constraints.
4) Laura to publish the final one-page runbook to the shared drive (link below) and confirm preflight test times.

Attachments included: final_runbook.md, updated capacity plan (20271109_demo_capacity_plan.xlsx).

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
